title: Types of Words
summary: The word classes of English and the system that links them: nouns, verbs, adjectives and adverbs.

lessons.title: The Word Classes
lessons.summary: Eight word classes, one system, and why the label matters.

steps.heading: Word Classes
steps.body: English groups words into classes, and the class of a word decides what it can do in a sentence. Nouns name people, places and things, verbs say what happens, adjectives describe, and adverbs modify. The same word often belongs to more than one class, which is why a dictionary gives several labels for a single entry. Learning the classes as a connected system is far more useful than treating them as four separate topics.

rules.title: The main classes
rules.statement: Every word in a sentence belongs to at least one word class, and the class is what determines its position and the words it combines with.
rules.formula: noun, verb, adjective, adverb, pronoun, preposition, conjunction, determiner

examples.en: The tall student answered the question quickly.
examples.vi: Học sinh cao lớn đã trả lời câu hỏi thật nhanh.
examples.note: noun: student, question; verb: answered; adjective: tall; adverb: quickly

rules.title: What a class tells you
rules.statement: A noun can be pluralised and takes a determiner, a verb takes a tense ending, an adjective has a comparative form, and an adverb usually ends in -ly.
rules.formula: book → books | work → works | quick → quicker | quick → quickly

examples.en: This is a quicker solution.
examples.vi: Đây là một cách giải quyết nhanh hơn.
examples.note: quick takes the comparative -er to become quicker

rules.title: One word, several classes
rules.statement: Many English words move between classes without any change in spelling, so the surrounding words decide the label.
rules.formula: fast (adjective / adverb) | light (noun / verb / adjective) | round (noun / verb / adjective / adverb)

examples.en: That was a fast train, and it ran fast.
examples.vi: Đó là một tàu nhanh, và nó chạy nhanh.
examples.note: the same word is an adjective in the first slot and an adverb in the second

examples.en: Nouns name: Hanoi, freedom, honesty.
examples.vi: Danh từ chỉ tên nơi chốn, sự tự do, sự trung thực.
examples.note: abstract and proper nouns count as nouns too

examples.en: Verbs act or state: run, build, believe.
examples.vi: Động từ nói về hành động hoặc trạng thái.
examples.note: verbs are the only words that carry tense

examples.en: Adjectives describe: a narrow street, a careless driver.
examples.vi: Tính từ miêu tả: con đường hẹp, một tài xế cẩu thả.
examples.note: adjectives usually sit before a noun or after a linking verb

examples.en: Adverbs modify: she sings beautifully.
examples.vi: Trạng từ bổ nghĩa: cô ấy hát rất hay.
examples.note: most adverbs end in -ly

examples.en: Function words hold the sentence together: the, of, and, but.
examples.vi: Từ chức năng giữ câu lại: the, of, and, but.
examples.note: a small closed set with no descriptive meaning of its own

exercises.prompt: Match each word to its word class in the sentence 'The careful driver stopped suddenly.'
exercises.instruction: Pair every word with the correct class.
exercises.explanation: Driver names a person, stopped is the action, careful describes the driver, suddenly modifies stopped, and The is a determiner that introduces the noun phrase. Together they show that one noun phrase carries a determiner, a noun and an adjective, followed by a verb phrase with a verb and an adverb.

exercises.prompt: In 'She sings beautifully', what class is 'beautifully'?
exercises.explanation: Beautifully modifies the verb sings, and any word that modifies a verb is an adverb. The -ly ending is a strong clue, since it is the standard way English forms adverbs of manner from adjectives.

exercises.prompt: Only verbs carry tense information such as past, present and future in English.
exercises.instruction: Decide whether the statement is true or false.
exercises.explanation: The statement is true. Nouns, adjectives and adverbs do not change with time, which is why a sentence like she sings and she sang differ in exactly one word. A learner who tries to conjugate a noun is looking for a pattern that English does not have.

exercises.prompt: The class that includes the, a and an is the ___ class.
exercises.explanation: The, a and an are determiners: they point at a noun and fix whether it is singular or plural. They are function words, because their job is grammatical rather than descriptive.

audio.text: The polite guide answered every question clearly.

acceptedAnswers: The polite guide answered every question clearly.
items.hint: determiner + adjective + noun + verb + noun + adverb
items.translation: Người hướng dẫn lịch sự đã trả lời mọi câu hỏi một cách rõ ràng.

audio.text: Honesty matters more than talent in the long run.

acceptedAnswers: Honesty matters more than talent in the long run.
items.hint: abstract nouns on both sides of a comparative
items.translation: Sự trung thực quan trọng hơn tài năng trong dài hạn.

questions.prompt: Which word is an adjective in this sentence? 'The old bridge was built quickly.'
questions.explanation: Old describes the bridge, so it is an adjective. Bridge is the noun, built is the verb, and quickly is an adverb because it modifies how the bridge was built rather than what kind of bridge it was.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence so that the classes are correct: 'The children played ___ in the garden.'
questions.explanation: The blank comes after the verb played, so it must be an adverb saying how the children played. An adjective such as happy cannot stand there without a linking verb, because English does not put an adjective straight after an action verb.

questions.prompt: Give the adjective form of the noun 'patience'.
questions.explanation: The adjective is patient, spelled exactly like the noun but used in a different slot: a patient person, and be patient. This kind of overlap is common in English and is why the surrounding words decide the class.

takeaways: Word classes decide what a word can do in a sentence.
Nouns name, verbs act or state, adjectives describe, adverbs modify.
Only verbs carry tense, and adverbs of manner usually end in -ly.
Many words belong to more than one class, and the surrounding words decide.

lessons.title: Nouns
lessons.summary: Countable and uncountable, singular and plural, common and proper.

steps.heading: Nouns
steps.body: Nouns name people, places, things, qualities and ideas, and they are the anchors that every other word in the sentence hangs off. English splits nouns into countable and uncountable, and the two behave differently with articles and plurals. Countable nouns have a singular and a plural; uncountable nouns do not, and to give them a number English uses a unit such as a piece of or an item of.

rules.title: Countable and uncountable
rules.statement: Countable nouns can be counted and have a plural. Uncountable nouns cannot be counted directly, so they take a quantifier instead of a or a number.
rules.formula: three books | some information, a piece of information

examples.en: I need three tickets for tonight's show.
examples.vi: Tôi cần ba vé cho buổi tối nay.
examples.note: tickets is countable and plural

examples.en: I need some information about the course.
examples.vi: Tôi cần một ít thông tin về khóa học.
examples.note: information is uncountable, so some replaces three

rules.title: Making plurals
rules.statement: Most nouns add -s. Nouns ending in -s, -x, -ch and -sh add -es, and nouns ending in a consonant plus y change the y to i and add -es.
rules.formula: book → books, box → boxes, city → cities

examples.en: The students answered three questions.
examples.vi: Các học sinh đã trả lời ba câu hỏi.
examples.note: question → questions

rules.title: Irregular and unchanged plurals
rules.statement: Some nouns have an irregular plural, some never change, and only a few have a distinct plural form used for a single object.
rules.formula: man → men, child → children | sheep, fish | knife → knives, foot → feet

examples.en: Three sheep were grazing near the fence.
examples.vi: Ba con cừu đang ăn cỏ gần hàng rào.
examples.note: sheep has the same form in singular and plural

examples.en: There is a lot of traffic this morning.
examples.vi: Sáng nay giao thông rất dày đặc.
examples.note: traffic is uncountable

examples.en: I bought two loaves of bread on the way home.
examples.vi: Trên đường về nhà tôi mua hai ổ bánh mì.
examples.note: uncountable noun with the unit loaves

examples.en: The children were playing in the garden.
examples.vi: Lũ trẻ đang chơi trong vườn.
examples.note: child → children, an irregular plural

examples.en: Hanoi is the capital of Vietnam.
examples.vi: Hà Nội là thủ đô của Việt Nam.
examples.note: a proper noun, always capitalised

examples.en: Could you give me some advice about the exam?
examples.vi: Bạn cho tôi một ít lời khuyên về kỳ thi được không?
examples.note: advice is uncountable and takes some, not a

exercises.prompt: I need two informations about the trip.

values: I need two pieces of information about the trip.

exercises.explanation: Information is uncountable, so it has no plural form and cannot be counted with two. English counts it with a unit noun: two pieces of information, or you can rephrase it as I need two items of information.

exercises.prompt: The plural of 'child' is ___.
exercises.explanation: Child has the irregular plural children, and the form is identical whether it takes a singular or a plural verb in meaning: the child is here, the children are here. There is no regular -s version in modern English.

exercises.prompt: friend
exercises.instruction: Write the plural of this noun.
exercises.explanation: Friend is regular, so the plural is simply friends with -s. Regular nouns are the large majority, which is why the -s form should always be your first guess before you look for an exception.

exercises.prompt: Which noun is uncountable?
exercises.explanation: Equipment is uncountable, so the sentence is some equipment or a piece of equipment, never equipments in the ordinary sense. The other three are ordinary countable nouns with regular plurals.

audio.text: The library bought three new dictionaries last month.

acceptedAnswers: The library bought three new dictionaries last month.
items.hint: dictionary ends in -y, so the plural is -ies
items.translation: Thư viện đã mua ba cuốn từ điển mới tháng trước.

audio.text: We need some advice about choosing a major.

acceptedAnswers: We need some advice about choosing a major.
items.hint: advice is uncountable and takes some
items.translation: Chúng tôi cần một ít lời khuyên về việc chọn ngành học.

questions.prompt: She gave me some good advices about my career.

values: She gave me some good advice about my career.

questions.explanation: Advice is uncountable in standard English, so it has no plural form and stays singular: some good advice. Speakers of some languages add a plural to abstract nouns, but English does not.

questions.prompt: Match each noun to the way it behaves with numbers.
questions.instruction: Pair every noun with the correct behaviour.
questions.explanation: A book and an apple can each be counted and have plurals, while water and luggage are measured rather than counted, so they take some or a piece of. Countability, not the meaning of the word, decides which group it falls into.

questions.prompt: Write the plural of the noun 'knife'.
questions.explanation: The plural of knife is knives, because the final f becomes v in the plural. The same change gives leaf → leaves and half → halves, and it is one of the few regular-looking patterns left in English plurals.

takeaways: Nouns name people, places, things, qualities and ideas.
Countable nouns have plurals; uncountable nouns take some or a piece of.
Most plurals add -s, with -es after -s, -x, -ch and -sh and -ies after consonant + y.
Sheep and fish keep the same form, and child → children and knife → knives are irregular.

lessons.title: Verbs
lessons.summary: Action and state verbs, main verbs, auxiliaries and transitivity.

steps.heading: Verbs
steps.body: Verbs are the heart of an English sentence, because they carry tense, voice and the relationship between the subject and what happens. The first split is action against state: a verb like build reports something you do, a verb like believe reports something you hold. The second split is main verbs against auxiliaries, where auxiliaries exist only to build tense, questions and negatives.

rules.title: Action and state verbs
rules.statement: Action verbs report a physical or mental activity. State verbs report a condition, a feeling or a possession, and they are usually not used in the continuous.
rules.formula: build, write, run | believe, own, belong, resemble

examples.en: They are building a new bridge.
examples.vi: Họ đang xây một cây cầu mới.
examples.note: an action verb, so the continuous is natural

examples.en: This bag belongs to my sister.
examples.vi: Chiếc túi này thuộc về chị tôi.
examples.note: a state verb, normally only in the simple form

rules.title: Main verbs and auxiliaries
rules.statement: A main verb carries the main meaning of the predicate. An auxiliary verb helps to build tense, the negative, the question or the passive, and it carries no meaning on its own.
rules.formula: be, have, do | will, can, must, would

examples.en: She has finished the work.
examples.vi: Cô ấy đã xong phần việc.
examples.note: has is the auxiliary, finished is the main verb

rules.title: Transitive and intransitive
rules.statement: A transitive verb needs an object, and an intransitive verb does not. Linking verbs are a third group, joining the subject to a word that renames or describes it.
rules.formula: She opened the window. | The flowers smell sweet. | He seems tired.

examples.en: The soup tastes delicious.
examples.vi: Món súp này nếm rất ngon.
examples.note: a linking verb, not a transitive verb with a missing object

examples.en: We must protect the environment.
examples.vi: Chúng ta phải bảo vệ môi trường.
examples.note: must is the auxiliary, protect is the main verb

examples.en: The children ran across the field.
examples.vi: Lũ trẻ chạy qua bãi cỏ.
examples.note: an intransitive action verb with no object

examples.en: He wrote a long letter to his friend.
examples.vi: Anh ấy đã viết một lá thư dài cho bạn.
examples.note: a transitive verb with the object a long letter

examples.en: The results are already known.
examples.vi: Kết quả đã được biết đến rồi.
examples.note: are is the auxiliary of the passive and known is the participle

examples.en: I didn't understand the question.
examples.vi: Tôi đã không hiểu câu hỏi.
examples.note: did is the auxiliary and understand is the base form main verb

exercises.prompt: Match each verb to its type.
exercises.instruction: Pair every verb with the correct type.
exercises.explanation: Build and write report something you do, so they are action verbs and accept the continuous: She is writing. Believe and own report a condition, so they are state verbs and stay in the simple form.

exercises.prompt: decision
exercises.instruction: Write the base verb related to this noun.
exercises.explanation: The verb is decide and the noun is decision, connected by the suffix -ion. Learning words in families of three, base, verb and noun, is a faster route to vocabulary than learning each item separately.

exercises.prompt: Auxiliary verbs such as have, do and can carry the main meaning of the sentence on their own.
exercises.instruction: Decide whether the statement is true or false.
exercises.explanation: The statement is false. Auxiliaries only support tense, negation, questions and the passive, so they need a main verb: she can, she can swim. A sentence that ends with an auxiliary is incomplete unless another verb follows.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence contains a transitive verb?
exercises.explanation: Opened takes the object the window, so it is transitive. The other three verbs take no object; loudly in option d is an adverb, not an object, which is a very common confusion.

audio.text: The committee has not yet published its report.

acceptedAnswers: The committee has not yet published its report.
items.hint: has is the auxiliary, published is the main verb
items.translation: Ủy ban chưa công bố báo cáo của mình.

items.hint: smell here is a linking verb
items.translation: Món súp này có mùi rất thơm.

questions.prompt: She is own a very expensive car.

values: She owns a very expensive car.

questions.explanation: Own is a state verb, and state verbs do not take the continuous, so the sentence is owns. This is the standard test: if the -ing form sounds odd, the verb is a state verb and the simple form is the only option.

questions.prompt: Match each verb to its role in the sentence.
questions.instruction: Pair every verb with the correct role.
questions.explanation: Have and was support the tense when a main verb such as finished or written follows, so they are auxiliaries here. Think and need carry the meaning of the clause on their own, so they are main verbs. The same word can change role between sentences.

questions.instruction: Write the base verb related to this adjective.
questions.explanation: The base verb is succeed, and the -ful suffix turns it into the adjective successful. The noun of the same family is success, so one root covers all three word classes.

takeaways: Action verbs report activities; state verbs report conditions and rarely take the continuous.
Main verbs carry meaning; auxiliaries such as be, have, do and the modals only support the grammar.
Transitive verbs need an object, intransitive verbs do not, and linking verbs join the subject to a description.
An adverb after a verb is not an object: he laughed loudly has no object at all.

lessons.title: Adjectives and Adverbs
lessons.summary: Position, order and the degree system that joins them.

steps.heading: Adjectives and Adverbs
steps.body: Adjectives describe nouns and pronouns, and they have a fixed set of positions: attributive before the noun, predicative after a linking verb, and postpositive in a few fixed phrases. Adverbs modify verbs, adjectives or whole adverbs, and the three types are named for what they modify. The two classes share one system of degree, so an adjective and the adverb derived from it behave in parallel.

rules.title: Adjective position
rules.statement: An adjective goes before the noun it describes, or after a linking verb when it describes the subject. A small set of fixed expressions puts it after the noun.
rules.formula: a narrow street | the street is narrow | the people present

examples.en: The room was small.
examples.vi: Căn phòng nhỏ.
examples.note: predicative position after the linking verb was

examples.en: The results were disappointing.
examples.vi: Kết quả rất đáng thất vọng.
examples.note: the noun is the subject, so the adjective follows the verb

rules.title: Types of adverb
rules.statement: Adverbs of manner say how, adverbs of place say where, adverbs of time says when, and adverbs of degree say how much.
rules.formula: She spoke softly. (manner) | He waited outside. (place) | They arrived early. (time) | It is extremely cold. (degree)

examples.en: The children played noisily in the garden.
examples.vi: Lũ trẻ chơi ồn ào trong vườn.
examples.note: noisily answers how they played, so it is an adverb of manner

rules.title: Adjective order
rules.statement: When several adjectives describe one noun, English normally puts them in a fixed order: opinion, size, age, shape, colour, origin, material, purpose.
rules.formula: a lovely small old round brown Italian wooden coffee table

examples.en: She bought a beautiful small black leather bag.
examples.vi: Cô ấy mua một chiếc túi da đen nhỏ xinh đẹp.
examples.note: opinion, size, colour, material

rules.title: Degree and the -ly link
rules.statement: An adjective and the adverb made from it share one degree system, so quick gives quicker, quickest, and quickly gives more quickly, most quickly.

examples.en: This is a faster road than the old one.
examples.vi: Đây là con đường nhanh hơn con đường cũ.
examples.note: faster is the comparative of the adjective fast

examples.en: The soup is very hot.
examples.vi: Món súp này rất nóng.
examples.note: an adjective after the linking verb is

examples.en: She explained the rule clearly.
examples.vi: Cô ấy đã giải thích quy tắc một cách rõ ràng.
examples.note: an adverb of manner modifying the verb explained

examples.en: The film was boring, so we left early.
examples.vi: Bộ phim chán nên chúng tôi ra về sớm.
examples.note: early modifies the verb left, so it is an adverb of time

examples.en: It is extremely difficult to explain.
examples.vi: Điều đó giải thích cực kỳ khó.
examples.note: extremely is an adverb of degree modifying the adjective difficult

examples.en: The new Japanese car is much more reliable.
examples.vi: Chiếc xe Nhật mới đáng tin hơn nhiều.
examples.note: more reliable compares the adjective, so the noun is reliable

exercises.prompt: The children are playing very noise in the garden.

values: The children are playing very noisily in the garden.

exercises.explanation: Noise is a noun, so it cannot modify the verb playing. The word that answers how the children played is the adverb noisily, and the -ly suffix is the standard marker that turns the adjective noisy into that adverb.

exercises.prompt: She sings ___ (beauty) than her sister.
exercises.instruction: Write the correct form of the word in brackets.
exercises.explanation: The blank modifies the verb sings, so it needs the adverb beautifully. Writing beautiful would describe a noun, and English does not put an adjective straight after an action verb without a linking verb.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order.
exercises.explanation: The order is size, age, material, purpose, so the phrase is a small old wooden table. The determiner always comes first and the head noun always comes last, and in between the adjectives follow the fixed English sequence.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
exercises.explanation: The word modifies the verb finished, so it must be the adverb quickly. Quick would describe a noun, quicker is a comparative and needs a than phrase, and quickful is not a word in English.

audio.text: The instructions were written very clearly.

acceptedAnswers: The instructions were written very clearly.
items.hint: adverb of manner after a passive verb
items.translation: Hướng dẫn được viết rất rõ ràng.

audio.text: It was an unusually cold winter this year.

acceptedAnswers: It was an unusually cold winter this year.
items.hint: adverb of degree before an adjective
items.translation: Mùa đông năm nay lạnh bất thường.

questions.prompt: Which word is an adverb in this sentence? 'The train arrived late again.'
questions.explanation: Late answers the question when the train arrived, so it modifies the verb and is an adverb. Again also modifies the verb, but the intended target here is the first time word, and both are functioning as adverbs of time.

questions.instruction: Write the adverb related to this adjective.
questions.explanation: Careful takes the -ly ending to give carefully, which describes how an action is performed. The suffix is the regular way English turns most adjectives into adverbs, and the same root also gives the noun carefulness.

questions.prompt: She speaks English more good than her brother.

values: She speaks English more well than her brother.

questions.explanation: The word modifies the verb speaks, so it needs the adverb well, and the comparative of well is better. Writing good uses the adjective where the adverb is required, and writing gooder is not a comparative because good already has the irregular form better.

takeaways: Adjectives describe nouns and go before the noun or after a linking verb.
Adverbs of manner, place, time and degree modify verbs, adjectives or other adverbs.
Adjectives in a row follow a fixed order: opinion, size, age, shape, colour, origin, material, purpose.
Adjective and adverb share one degree system: quick, quicker, quickest; quickly, more quickly.

lessons.title: Function Words and Content Words
lessons.summary: A closed set of structural words against an open set of meaningful ones.

steps.heading: Function Words and Content Words
steps.body: English splits its vocabulary into a small closed set of function words and an open set of content words. Function words such as the, of, and, is, to and at carry grammar rather than meaning, and there are only a few hundred of them in total. Content words carry the meaning of the sentence, and new ones can be invented at any time, which is why technology news is full of nouns nobody has used before.

rules.title: The two sets
rules.statement: Function words are a fixed list that is effectively closed. Content words are open and grow all the time, and they are mostly nouns, verbs, adjectives and adverbs.
rules.formula: the, a, an, of, in, on, at, to, for, and, or, but, is, was, do, have | run, hospital, quick, quietly

examples.en: The children quietly left the room.
examples.vi: Lũ trẳm lặng rời khỏi căn phòng.
examples.note: the, of the, is a function word; children, quietly and left are content words

rules.title: Why the split matters
rules.statement: Function words carry the relationships in a sentence: who did what to whom, and when. Remove them and the content words lose their grammar.
rules.formula: I saw her. → I saw her / I saw her and him

examples.en: She gave the book to him.
examples.vi: Cô ấy đưa cuốn sách cho anh ấy.
examples.note: to him is entirely function words and pronouns, and it carries the direction

rules.title: Auxiliaries as function words
rules.statement: The auxiliary verbs be, do and have only count as function words when they support the grammar. As a main verb, be is a content word because it has a meaning of its own.
rules.formula: She is here. (be = main verb, content word) | She is working. (be = auxiliary, function word)

examples.en: The book is on the table.
examples.vi: Cuốn sách nằm trên bàn.
examples.note: here is is a linking verb with a meaning of its own

examples.en: Although it was cheap, the phone broke after a month.
examples.vi: Mặc dù rẻ, chiếc điện thoại hỏng sau một tháng.
examples.note: although and but are both function words expressing contrast

examples.en: She works at a hospital near the river.
examples.vi: Cô ấy làm việc ở một bệnh viện gần sông.
examples.note: at, a and near are structural; hospital and river carry the meaning

examples.en: I couldn't find it, so I asked again.
examples.vi: Tôi không tìm thấy nó, nên tôi hỏi lại.
examples.note: couldn't, so and again do little or no lexical work

examples.en: The conference will be held in Da Nang next March.
examples.vi: Hội nghị sẽ được tổ chức ở Đà Nẵng vào tháng Ba tới.
examples.note: will be holds the tense and the passive, not a meaning

examples.en: Few people understand quantum computing.
examples.vi: Ít người hiểu lĩnh vực điện toán lượng tử.
examples.note: content words can be brand new; the grammar around them is fixed

exercises.prompt: Which words in 'The book is on the desk' are function words? Select all that apply.
exercises.explanation: The, is and on are the structure of the sentence: they show which noun, build the tense and give the position. Book and desk are the content words, and they are the part a listener must actually understand.

exercises.prompt: Match each word to the group it belongs to.
exercises.instruction: Pair every word with the correct group.
exercises.explanation: Because and with connect and relate, which is grammar rather than meaning, so they are function words. Quickly and happiness carry lexical content, and English could survive without them in a sentence but not without the connectors.

exercises.prompt: Function words are a fixed set, while content words can be added to English over time.
exercises.instruction: Decide whether the statement is true or false.
exercises.explanation: The statement is true. The function word list is effectively closed, whereas new content words enter English constantly, and any new noun or verb can be built from existing suffixes. That is why English can describe a new invention without rebuilding its grammar.

exercises.prompt: The conference will held in Da Nang.

values: The conference will be held in Da Nang.

exercises.explanation: The passive needs both halves: the auxiliary will and be, then the participle held. Dropping the auxiliary leaves the sentence with no tense, which is why learners who leave out will must also add be.

audio.text: Although the ticket was expensive, we enjoyed the concert.

acceptedAnswers: Although the ticket was expensive, we enjoyed the concert.
items.hint: function words open the clause and mark the contrast
items.translation: Mặc dù vé đắt, chúng tôi vẫn rất thích buổi hòa nhạc.

audio.text: They have already moved into the new apartment.

acceptedAnswers: They have already moved into the new apartment.
items.hint: have is an auxiliary, not a main verb
items.translation: Họ đã chuyển vào căn hộ mới rồi.

questions.prompt: Which group contains only function words?
questions.explanation: Of, the, and and is all do grammatical work and none of them carries an independent meaning. The other options each sneak in a content word, which is the usual way this question is set: the trap is a list that looks purely structural until you read it properly.

Results cannot announce anything, so the sentence needs the passive: were announced, which uses the past auxiliary were plus the participle. The original uses have with a base verb after it, which is the shape English never produces.

questions.instruction: Write the noun formed from this adjective.
questions.explanation: The suffix -ity turns the adjective reliable into the noun reliability. The untrustworthy opposite is unreliability, and the same suffixes build whole families of content words from one root.

takeaways: Function words are a small closed set that carries grammar: the, of, and, is, to, at.
Content words carry meaning and the set is open, so new words enter English all the time.
Auxiliaries such as be, do and have are function words only when they support the grammar.
Learners usually know the function words first and the content words second, which is why comprehension lags behind production.

lessons.title: Word Classes in Real Sentences
lessons.summary: One word in several classes, and how position settles the ambiguity.

steps.heading: Ambiguity and Word Class in Context
steps.body: At an advanced level the interesting problem is the word that could belong to more than one class. A dictionary lists every class a word can take, and the surrounding words decide which one applies. Recognising the ambiguity is the point, because it explains both why a sentence is wrong and why a second, equally correct reading exists.

rules.title: Noun or verb
rules.statement: Many words such as light, water, book, name and answer work as both. The slot decides: a determiner before it usually means noun, while a subject or a tense ending usually means verb.
rules.formula: a light bulb (noun) | light the room (verb)

examples.en: Please water the plants while we are away.
examples.vi: Xin bạn tưới cây trong lúc chúng tôi vắng mặt.
examples.note: water as a verb, taking the object the plants

rules.title: Adjective or adverb
rules.statement: A small group of words serves both classes with no change in form. The presence of a verb to modify makes the adverb reading likely.

examples.en: He works hard and plays hard too.
examples.vi: Anh ấy làm việc chăm chỉ và cũng chơi hết mình.
examples.note: hard modifies the verbs works and plays, so both are adverbs

rules.title: -ing as noun or verb
rules.statement: The -ing form is a noun when it names an activity and a verb when it is part of a larger clause, and the test is whether you can put a determiner in front of it.
rules.formula: Swimming is good exercise. (noun) | She is swimming. (verb)

examples.en: Reading before bed helps me relax.
examples.vi: Đọc sách trước khi ngủ giúp tôi thư giãn.
examples.note: a determiner could be placed before reading, so it is a noun here

examples.en: The book is on the shelf; I read it last night.
examples.vi: Cuốn sách nằm trên kệ, tôi đã đọc nó đêm qua.
examples.note: book is a noun in the first clause and a verb in the second

examples.en: She sings beautifully in three languages.
examples.vi: Cô ấy hát rất hay bằng ba thứ tiếng.
examples.note: the adverb and the numeral modifier both work

examples.en: He answered the question with a single word.
examples.vi: Anh ấy trả lời câu hỏi bằng một từ duy nhất.
examples.note: answer as a verb and word as a noun

examples.en: Locking the door takes only a second.
examples.vi: Việc khóa cửa chỉ mất một giây.
examples.note: locking is the subject noun, so the verb takes the singular form

examples.en: A light dinner is enough for me.
examples.vi: Một bữa tối nhẹ là đủ với tôi.
examples.note: light as an adjective describing the dinner

exercises.prompt: Match each word to the class it has in the sentence given.
exercises.instruction: Pair every word with the correct class.
exercises.explanation: The same spelling can carry different classes and the neighbouring words decide. In a light dinner the determiner a and the noun dinner make light an adjective, while light the room has an object, which only a verb can take.

exercises.prompt: success
exercises.instruction: Write the base verb related to this noun.
exercises.explanation: The verb is succeed, the noun is success and the adjective is successful, built with the -ion and -ful suffixes. A word family is the fastest way to acquire several word classes at once, and the suffix tells you which class you are holding.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order.
exercises.explanation: The order is subject, auxiliary, adverb, main verb, then the prepositional phrase to English. The adverb has to come before the main verb, not after the whole clause, which is the point this exercise tests.

exercises.prompt: Swimming are good exercise for the heart.

values: Swimming is good exercise for the heart.

exercises.explanation: The -ing form is a noun here because it names an activity and a determiner could stand in front of it, and a gerund subject is singular, so the verb is is. Reading is a good exercise would be the alternative if you wanted to keep the plural.

exercises.prompt: Which words can work as a verb in some sentence? Select all that apply.
exercises.explanation: Light and water are both nouns and verbs, so you can light the room and water the plants. Careful and beautiful are adjectives only, which is why they can never appear in a subject position before a verb.

audio.text: Please water the plants before you leave the flat.

acceptedAnswers: Please water the plants before you leave the flat.
items.hint: water as a verb with the object the plants
items.translation: Xin bạn tưới cây trước khi rời khỏi căn hộ.

audio.text: Learning a new language takes patience more than talent.

acceptedAnswers: Learning a new language takes patience more than talent.
items.hint: a gerund noun as the subject, so the verb is singular
items.translation: Học ngôn ngữ mới cần sự kiên nhẫn hơn là tài năng.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses 'round' as a verb?

items.text: She rounded the number to the nearest ten.

questions.explanation: Option a gives round an object, the number, which only a verb can take. In option b and option d round describes a noun, and in option c it modifies the numeral as an adverb of approximation.

questions.prompt: He is a very carefully driver, but his brother drives more careless.

values: He is a very careful driver, but his brother drives more carelessly.

questions.explanation: Carefully is an adverb and cannot describe the noun driver, so the adjective careful is needed before it. After the verb drives the word must be the adverb carelessly, and the comparative of carelessly is formed with more.

questions.instruction: Write the adjective related to this verb.
questions.explanation: Helpful is the adjective, formed with the -ful suffix, and the noun helpfulness belongs to the same family. The class of the word changes with the suffix, and the suffix tells you which class you have built.

takeaways: Many words belong to more than one class, and the surrounding words decide which applies.
A determiner before a word usually signals a noun; an object after it usually signals a verb.
The -ing form is a noun when it names an activity and a verb when it is part of a clause.
Word families give you several classes at once: succeed, success, successful, successfully.
